integrity: The lower boundary is a complete exact enumeration of every positive-cell integer confusion matrix through seven observations within each fixed-prevalence slice. The persistent family is proved by explicit rational F1 differences and exact factorizations of the squared-Matthews comparison, with an independent standard-library replay.
scientific_limitations: The theorem is restricted to hard binary classifications compared at common sample size and common actual-positive count, with every confusion-matrix cell positive. It is an ordinal point-estimate statement and does not address uncertainty, threshold optimization, calibration, multiclass averaging, or zero-cell conventions.
title: Seven cases are the sharp F1–Matthews ranking boundary
